# cargoship_cluster (Resource)

A Kubernetes cluster cargoship installs, joins and upgrades. One resource holds every host: cargoship takes a cluster-wide lock and starts controllers in a batch of one for quorum, so a resource per node would contend on the lock and lose the ordering batching expresses.

An apply converges the cluster on the configuration. There is no separate install and upgrade: the engine version already on each host is what tells one from the other, and a downgrade is refused rather than attempted.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cargoship_cluster" "prod" {
  name          = "prod-cluster"
  load_balancer = "10.0.0.10"
  package       = "/srv/staging/k3s-v1.33.4.tar.zst"

  profiles = {
    control = {
      node_labels = { "purpose-control" = "true" }
      ports       = [{ port = "6443" }]
      concurrency = "1"
    }
    worker = {
      node_labels = { "purpose-worker" = "true" }
    }
  }

  values = yamlencode({
    addons = {
      disabled = ["traefik"]
    }
  })

  hosts = {
    controller1 = {
      address  = "10.0.0.11"
      role     = "controller"
      key_path = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
      profile  = "control"
    }

    worker1 = {
      address  = "10.0.0.21"
      role     = "worker"
      key_path = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
      profile  = "worker"
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `load_balancer` (String) The address clients use to reach the control plane.
- `name` (String) The cluster's name. It becomes `metadata.name` and the kubeconfig context, and changing it replaces the cluster.
- `package` (String) The distro package to install: a path to a `.tar.zst` built by `cargoship package create`, or an OCI reference. A package reference is resolved when the apply runs, so an airgapped management node wants a path.

### Optional

- `allow_downgrade` (Boolean) Continue when a host already runs an engine newer than the package carries. A downgrade is refused by default, because an engine does not support being moved backwards.
- `allow_unmanaged_nodes` (Boolean) Continue when the cluster holds a node no `hosts` entry accounts for. An apply removes nothing, so by default a node left behind by a deleted entry stops the run.
- `export_kubeconfig` (Boolean) Return the cluster's admin credentials in the `kubeconfig` attribute. It is off by default and should stay off unless something in the configuration consumes it: the credentials are cluster-admin, and any computed attribute lands in the state file whether or not it is marked sensitive. `cargoship install kube-config` writes a kubeconfig without putting one in state.
- `hosts` (Attributes Map) The fleet, keyed by hostname or an identifier of your choosing. The key names the host when `hostname` is not set, and it is what orders the run: controllers are acted on first, and the controller whose key sorts first becomes the leader. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hosts))
- `label_nodes` (Boolean) Add the `node-role.kubernetes.io/<profile>` label to each node, from the host's `profile`.
- `modify_firewall` (Boolean) Rewrite the host firewall (firewalld, ufw or nftables) with the engine's rules.
- `modify_hosts` (Boolean) Rewrite `/etc/hosts` on every host with the cluster's own nodes.
- `no_drain_on_destroy` (Boolean) Skip draining each node before it is deleted during a destroy. Faster, and it gives workloads no chance to move.
- `profiles` (Attributes Map) The profiles a host can select, keyed by name. A profile is how a fleet says "every infra node is tainted this way" once rather than per host, and it is also where per-profile concurrency is set.

A host's own `node_labels`, `node_taints` and `ports` **replace** its profile's rather than merging with them; firewall rules are the exception and are unioned. A host that selects a profile this map does not define is a configuration error, since the labels and taints it expected would otherwise silently never exist. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--profiles))
- `retain_on_destroy` (Boolean) Leave the cluster running when the resource is destroyed, dropping it from state with a warning instead of resetting it. Destroying resets by default, because that is what destroy means everywhere else.
- `timeout` (String) How long the phases wait for a host to reach the state they want, as a Go duration (`20m`). It bounds the retry loops inside a run, not the run itself.
- `values` (String) Overrides for the values the distro package was built with, as a YAML string (e.g. from `file("values.yaml")` or `yamlencode(...)`).
- `values_files` (List of String) Paths to YAML values files overriding the values the package ships with. Loaded and merged in order, winning over inline `values`.
- `worker_concurrency` (String) How many workers are installed or upgraded at a time, as a count (`5`) or a percentage of the batch (`25%`).

### Read-Only

- `distro` (String) The engine the package carries, read from the package rather than stated twice. It is what a later refresh and a destroy need.
- `engine_version` (String) The engine version the package carries.
- `id` (String) The cluster's name, which is its identity here. There is no `import`: the `hosts` entries and their key paths are not recoverable from a running cluster.
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) The cluster's admin credentials, populated only when `export_kubeconfig` is set.
- `nodes` (Attributes List) What each host reported during the run, in the order the apply acted on them: controllers first. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nodes))

<a id="nestedatt--hosts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hosts`

Required:

- `address` (String) The address or hostname cargoship opens an SSH connection to.
- `role` (String) The host's role: one of `controller`, `controller+worker`, `single`, `worker`.

Optional:

- `bastion` (Attributes) The jump host this host is reached through. Cargoship opens its own SSH connections, so a bastion has to be stated here rather than inherited from an SSH client configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hosts--bastion))
- `environment` (Map of String) Environment variables cargoship sets on the host, for a proxy or a no-proxy list.
- `firewall_rules` (Attributes List) Firewall rules for this host. Unlike the fields above, these are unioned with the profile's rather than replacing them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hosts--firewall_rules))
- `hostname` (String) The name the host is known by before it has been visited.
- `key_path` (String) Path to the SSH private key on the machine running OpenTofu. There is no attribute for key material, and there will not be: a key in the configuration is a key in the state file.
- `node_labels` (Map of String) Kubernetes node labels for this host. They **replace** the labels of the profile the host selects rather than merging with them.
- `node_taints` (List of String) Kubernetes node taints for this host, as `key=value:Effect`. They replace the profile's rather than merging with them.
- `port` (Number) The SSH port. Defaults to 22.
- `ports` (Attributes List) Ports opened on this host, replacing the profile's. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hosts--ports))
- `private_address` (String) Overrides the private address the facts phase would discover.
- `private_interface` (String) Overrides the private interface the facts phase would discover, for a node with more than one.
- `profile` (String) The profile this host selects from the cluster's profile map, which also becomes its `node-role.kubernetes.io/<profile>` label when `label_nodes` is set.
- `state` (String) The lifecycle state of this host: `present` (the default) or `absent`. Marking a host `absent` drains it, deletes it from the cluster and uninstalls its engine on the next apply, while every other host keeps running.

The block stays where it is afterwards -- `removed` records that the work is done, so later applies leave the machine alone and never try to reach one that has been decommissioned. Delete the block whenever it suits; nothing depends on it going.

Removal is stated rather than inferred from a deleted block, because deleting the block takes the address and the key path with it: see [choice-removed-hosts](https://github.com/colonel-byte/cargoship/blob/main/docs/agent/choice-removed-hosts.md).
- `user` (String) The SSH user. Defaults to `root`.

Read-Only:

- `removed` (Boolean) Whether this host has been removed from the cluster. Computed: it becomes true once a host marked `absent` has been torn down, and that is what stops the removal from running again.

<a id="nestedatt--hosts--bastion"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hosts.bastion`

Required:

- `address` (String) The bastion's address.

Optional:

- `key_path` (String) Path to the private key for the bastion, on the machine running OpenTofu.
- `port` (Number) The SSH port on the bastion. Defaults to 22.
- `user` (String) The SSH user on the bastion. Defaults to `root`.


<a id="nestedatt--hosts--firewall_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hosts.firewall_rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) What happens to matching traffic: `allow`, `deny` or `reject`. It is the one field a rule cannot omit.

Optional:

- `destination` (String) The address or CIDR the traffic goes to.
- `direction` (String) `in`, `out` or `forward`. Defaults to `in`.
- `egress` (String) Where forward traffic leaves, read the same way as `ingress`. Forward rules only.
- `ingress` (String) Where forward traffic enters: a zone on firewalld hosts, an interface on ufw hosts. Forward rules only.
- `name` (String) Names the rule, and names the artifacts cargoship writes on the node for it, so it has to be unique within a host. One is generated when it is empty.
- `port` (String) The port or inclusive range the rule matches.
- `protocol` (String) The protocol the rule matches.
- `source` (String) The address or CIDR the traffic comes from.


<a id="nestedatt--hosts--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hosts.ports`

Required:

- `port` (String) The port number or inclusive range, as a string: `6443`, `30000-32767`.

Optional:

- `protocol` (String) `tcp` or `udp`. Defaults to `tcp`.



<a id="nestedatt--profiles"></a>
### Nested Schema for `profiles`

Optional:

- `concurrency` (String) How many hosts sharing this profile cargoship acts on at once -- draining, upgrading, initializing, uninstalling -- as a count (`1`) or a percentage of those hosts (`25%`). Empty falls back to the phase's own concurrency.
- `firewall_rules` (Attributes List) Firewall rules applied to a host selecting this profile. A host's own rules are unioned with these rather than replacing them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--profiles--firewall_rules))
- `node_labels` (Map of String) Kubernetes node labels applied to a host selecting this profile.
- `node_taints` (List of String) Kubernetes node taints applied to a host selecting this profile, as `key=value:Effect`.
- `ports` (Attributes List) Ports opened on a host selecting this profile. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--profiles--ports))

<a id="nestedatt--profiles--firewall_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `profiles.firewall_rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) What happens to matching traffic: `allow`, `deny` or `reject`. It is the one field a rule cannot omit.

Optional:

- `destination` (String) The address or CIDR the traffic goes to.
- `direction` (String) `in`, `out` or `forward`. Defaults to `in`.
- `egress` (String) Where forward traffic leaves, read the same way as `ingress`. Forward rules only.
- `ingress` (String) Where forward traffic enters: a zone on firewalld hosts, an interface on ufw hosts. Forward rules only.
- `name` (String) Names the rule, and names the artifacts cargoship writes on the node for it, so it has to be unique within a host. One is generated when it is empty.
- `port` (String) The port or inclusive range the rule matches.
- `protocol` (String) The protocol the rule matches.
- `source` (String) The address or CIDR the traffic comes from.


<a id="nestedatt--profiles--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `profiles.ports`

Required:

- `port` (String) The port number or inclusive range, as a string: `6443`, `30000-32767`.

Optional:

- `protocol` (String) `tcp` or `udp`. Defaults to `tcp`.



<a id="nestedatt--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nodes`

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) The address cargoship connected to.
- `arch` (String) The CPU architecture the host reports.
- `engine_version` (String) The engine version running on the host, or `v0.0.0` for a host with no engine installed. This is the value a plan-time downgrade check compares a package against.
- `hostname` (String) The hostname the host reports.
- `os` (String) The `ID` from the host's os-release.
- `os_version` (String) The `VERSION_ID` from the host's os-release.
- `private_address` (String) The private address cargoship discovered, or the one the host block declared.
- `role` (String) The role the host block gave it.
